ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Arts. L.561-1 to L.561-50; R.561-1 to R.561-59; Code de commerce Arts. L.123-1 et seq., L.233-3; Décret n° 2017-1094 du 12 juin 2017; Arrêté du 12 juin 2017; EU AMLD4/5/6 transposed; TRACFIN, ACPR, and INPI RBE regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Good Standing of foreign parent
Board Resolution authorizing incorporation and appointing signatory
Power of Attorney for French incorporation agent
Passport copies and proof of residence of directors/shareholders/UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport authority / utility or bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Tax Residency of foreign parent
Sworn French translation of all foreign-language documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized translation attached to apostilled original

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / source of funds declaration

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against EU Consolidated Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and SSI lists, French Registre national des gels (asset freeze), PEP databases, and French TRACFIN guidance. Enhanced due diligence for Medium_Risk_Enhanced: verify UBO chain, adverse media, source of funds/wealth, senior PEP approval, annual refresh; report suspicious transactions to TRACFIN without delay.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI) – https://procedures.inpi.fr; RCS via Infogreffe; INPI data.inpi.fr for name availability.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French must be used for company name, corporate documents, and filings (Loi Toubon; Code de commerce Art. L.123-5). Foreign names must be transliterated into Latin script; non-Latin scripts require certified French translation. Name must include 'SAS' or 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' and cannot be misleading or infringe prior rights. INPI certificate of availability is advisory, valid 3 months, not a statutory reservation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If INPI/greffe rejects name, obtain written rejection notice. File recours gracieux with the competent greffier or INPI within 30 days, submitting alternate names and trademark search. If maintained, file recours contentieux before the Tribunal judiciaire within 2 months of rejection. Parallel: secure EU/French trademark clearance and domain names.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is generally not accepted for industrial manufacturing, export, or AML medium-risk enhanced activities. A domiciliation contract with an authorized domiciliataire is permitted for the registered office under Code de commerce Arts. L.123-11-2 et seq., but tax and customs authorities require substantive operational presence (employees, premises, equipment) for SAS active optics manufacturing. Virtual-only address may trigger permanent establishment, CFC, and substance challenges.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: 25–35% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection by URSSAF, DREETS, French Customs (DGDDI), DGFiP, and ACPR/TRACFIN given manufacturing, dual-use optics, and export payment rails.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Articles L. 210-1 to L. 210-10, L. 227-1 to L. 227-20, and R. 227-1 et seq.; applicable implementing provisions set out in the Code de commerce and Code de l'environnement where physical licensing is relevant.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), administered by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; corporate formalities are transmitted through the Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts d'Incorporation signés (Article of Association executed by all founding shareholders) together with the standardized registration dossier transmitted through INPI's Guichet unique (the RCS immatriculation file); upon completion the Greffe issues an official Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital is imposed for a Société par Actions Simplifiée. If the Articles fix a positive share capital, all shares must be fully subscribed and at least 50% of cash contributions must be paid up before registration; the balance may be called within five years unless the Articles provide otherwise. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked escrow account opened in the company's name (usually with a French bank or a notary as séquestre) and a certificate of blocked funds must be delivered to the registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The undersigned founding shareholder approves subscription and full allocation of the issued share capital set out in the Articles of Association. The registered office shall be situated at [address], and the President shall have broad powers to represent the Company subject to law and the Articles. The shareholder appoints [name] as President and [name] as Director of Operations, with authority to execute all regulatory filings and sign documents before the competent registry. The President is authorized to open bank accounts and complete all incorporation formalities, and orders that this resolution be recorded and maintained as a corporate act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-formation name clearance and structuring review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI national database and Infogreffe RCS index; non-binding consultation through the Guichet unique portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the proposed corporate name, domain name, and trademark availability on the RCS and INPI registries. Confirm the exact SAS corporate purpose in French, including manufacture of precision optical glass lenses, camera modules, and related optical assemblies. If desired, file a trademark application with INPI before incorporation to protect the trade name.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and purpose in French or English with a certified translation
Identity documents of all founding shareholders
Anticipated share capital structure and contribution report if in-kind assets are used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS registration, submit a revised name and request a fresh conflict check before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SAS Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate counsel; notary public in remit where real-property contributions or legally registered in-kind contributions are involved.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles in French, prescribing corporate purpose, registered office, legal form, share capital, rights attached to securities, management rules, shareholder decision procedure, and duration not exceeding 99 years. Have each founding shareholder sign every page and the final page. If a contribution consists of immovable property or shares subject to public registration, execute before a notary and appoint a Commissaire aux Apports to file a contribution report.
required_dossiers: SAS Articles of Association in French
Shareholder identity documents and proof of residence
List of named shareholders with subscribed and paid-up amounts
Contribution agreements and Commissaire aux Apports report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary, registry, or reviewer observes defects, amend and re-execute the Articles or file supplementary statements through the Guichet unique within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of subscribed cash capital in a blocked account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French licensed bank or notary acting as séquestre; Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations when escrow is used.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary company bank account under the name of the SAS in formation and deposit at least 50% of the authorized cash share capital, or the full amount if the Articles require immediate full payment. Ensure the depositary issues a formal attestation stating the funds are blocked until incorporation and available to the President upon RCS registration. Obtain the bank account certificate, which must be attached to the registration file.
required_dossiers: Application for a French bank account in the company's name
Notarized or private signature specimen of the future President and any co-signatories
Anti-money-laundering KYC file for each beneficial owner
Deposit receipt or blocked-funds certificate issued by the bank or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries KYC or the source of funds, provide certified beneficial-ownership evidence and transactional documentation; if the account is denied, obtain a notary escrow certificate from a French notary instead.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the incorporation dossier through the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); final review by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the INPI Guichet unique and electronically submit the standardized formalities file, including the M0 form, signed Articles, bank certificate, appointment documents, declaration of compliance, and beneficial-owner declaration. Pay the applicable registry and ancillary fees online. The Greffe examines the file and issues observations or registers the company in the RCS.
required_dossiers: Standardized registration form confirmed by INPI (M0 form)
Signed SAS Articles of Association
Bank or notary certificate of capital deposit
Declaration of beneficial shareholders (Declaration des Beneficiaires Effectifs) form
Standard compliance declaration signed by the President
Evidence of power of attorney, if a representative is submitting
Consent to registered office address or domiciliation agreement
Identity documents and any required non-conviction declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a observation, respond through the Guichet unique within 15 days by amending the defective document or producing the missing evidence; if the file is rejected, correct and resubmit the affected attachments without resetting previously valid parts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Kbis extract, SIREN identification and administrative identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and INSEE via the electronic RCS/INSEE interconnection.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation, obtain the official Kbis extract, which is the conclusive certificate of incorporation. Confirm that the SIREN, SIRET, and NAF/APE code have been assigned; for precision optical manufacturing and camera modules, the appropriate APE/NAF code is 26.70Z. Verify the VAT registration number has been automatically transmitted to DGFiP; if not, request allocation through the tax authorities.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract or RCS registration notification
SIREN/SIRET assignment notice
NAF/APE code classification notice
Automatic VAT number or DGFiP VAT-related notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NAF code is misallocated or the VAT number is not received, submit a correction request to INSEE and the local tax administration through DGFiP's professional online portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of incorporation notice and post-registration tax and social formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal announcement gazette (Support d'annonces légales), DGFiP (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques), and URSSAF if initial employees are enrolled.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the mandatory notice of incorporation in an authorized legal journal in the jurisdiction of the registered office, including the company form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, and the President's identity. Enroll the company with DGFiP for corporate income tax, VAT, property tax, and administrative accounts; request an inter-company SIRET and employer registration if employees will be hired. Appoint a statutory auditor only if the legal thresholds are met, and maintain the corporate minute book as prescribed.
required_dossiers: Published incorporation notice in an approved legal journal
Kbis extract
DGFiP tax registration forms
URSSAF employer registration form, if applicable
Consent of the President and any corporate officers
Initial corporate minutes and share register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal gazette contains errors, publish a correction note and transmit the rectified publication to the Greffe; if DGFiP or URSSAF response is delayed, use the RCS Kbis and declaration receipts as proof of existence while completing the relevant supplementary declaration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) acting through the inspection des installations classées, together with the local Préfecture for environmental authorization decisions.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation environnementale or Enregistrement ICPE, as applicable; no separate optical-lens manufacturing business license is generally required, but the operator must be compliant with environmental and occupational safety requirements before production commences.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), with the competent Préfecture as the issuing authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Enregistrement) or Authorization (Autorisation environnementale) under Articles L. 511-1 et seq. of the Code de l'environnement when processes reach ICPE thresholds (e.g., degreasing, surface treatment or organic-solvent consumption); below the threshold the facility is non-ICPE and may proceed without a preliminary environmental permit, subject to general municipal and zoning requirements.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Where process wastewater is discharged to a public sewer, the effluent must respect the general thresholds of the applied municipal authorization and good practice limits: pH 5.5-8.5, BOD5 ≤ 35 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L, and no free halogenated hydrocarbons. Solvent and VOC emissions shall be controlled under the Solvent Emissions Directive transposition, including substitution of hazardous solvents, abatement systems, and compliance with occupational exposure limits where annual solvent consumption exceeds the statutory threshold.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety clearance and workplace compliance are required: obtain a building permit or planning certificate for new or modified industrial premises; obtain a structural-load inspection certificate from an approved technical control office (e.g., Bureau Veritas, SOCOTEC, Apave) confirming the floor can support installed equipment; obtain fire-safety verification covering accessible evacuation routes, extinguishing systems, emergency lighting, and alarm devices; and secure Code du travail occupational clearance confirming ventilation, noise, electrical safety, and sanitary facilities meet French workplace standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), principally through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the Non-Resident Tax Department (Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères, SIEE) where applicable. Main digital services are available through the official impots.gouv.fr business tax portal. Legal entities are incorporated through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), with resulting registration in the Registre national des entreprises (RNE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS normally obtains its SIREN and SIRET identifiers through the Guichet unique incorporation filing. The SIREN is the core legal-entity identifier and is used in tax administration. A French VAT identification number is issued by the competent SIE and generally has the format FR followed by two check characters and the nine-digit SIREN. The company must file incorporation and tax-registration information, identify its registered office, legal representatives, activities, accounting period, bank details, and VAT regime, and provide constitutional documents and beneficial-owner information where requested. A non-resident entity without a French establishment applies to the SIEE or otherwise competent SIE for a French VAT number before carrying out transactions requiring French VAT registration. The application normally includes the foreign certificate of incorporation, tax-residence certificate, articles or equivalent constitutional documents, proof of business activity, representative details, bank information, and evidence supporting the intended French taxable transactions. EU-established applicants may generally use the applicable electronic VAT-registration and administrative-assistance channels. VAT registration is not automatically required where French reverse-charge rules apply to all relevant supplies, but the entity must maintain evidence supporting that conclusion.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) by default. A qualifying SAS may elect for taxation at shareholder level under the French income-tax regime (impôt sur le revenu, IR) for a maximum period of five fiscal years, subject to statutory conditions, including generally being newly created, unlisted, below the applicable employee and turnover or balance-sheet limits, and meeting ownership and management participation requirements. The election must be made within the statutory period and notified to the tax authority. There is no general U.S.-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid rules under the Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework can deny deductions or impose inclusion consequences for hybrid mismatches; they do not provide a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT) under the French General Tax Code and EU VAT framework.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For established French businesses using the domestic VAT exemption regime, the principal turnover thresholds are generally EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and certain accommodation or catering activities and EUR 37,500 for services, with increased tolerance thresholds generally of EUR 93,500 and EUR 41,250 respectively. These thresholds are subject to statutory activity-specific rules and annual legislative changes. They do not generally protect a non-established business making French-taxable supplies: such a business may require VAT registration from the first taxable transaction unless a reverse-charge, place-of-supply, or other statutory exception applies. Intra-Community acquisition thresholds and distance-selling rules are separate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for all domestic business invoices. Invoices must satisfy French VAT and accounting requirements, including issuer and customer identity, valid VAT numbers where relevant, invoice date and sequential number, description, taxable amount, VAT rate and amount, exemptions or reverse-charge wording, and payment terms. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for transactions with French public-sector bodies through the Chorus Pro system. The broader domestic business-to-business reform provides for mandatory receipt of electronic invoices by all businesses from 1 September 2026, with mandatory issuance generally from 1 September 2026 for large and medium-sized businesses and from 1 September 2027 for small and micro-enterprises, subject to legislative implementation and permitted extensions. Invoices will be exchanged through approved private platforms or the public invoicing portal, with transaction and payment data reporting to the tax administration. Digital integrity may be established through qualified electronic signature, a reliable audit trail, or an approved electronic data interchange process; ordinary invoices are not generally subject to individual tax-authority digital stamping before issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched from France to a destination outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT under Article 262 of the French General Tax Code if the supplier is the exporter or acts in the legally permitted export structure and obtains evidence that the goods left the EU customs territory. The supplier must retain the customs export declaration and an electronic exit result or equivalent customs evidence, together with commercial, transport, and accounting records linking the goods to the transaction. Intra-Community supplies of goods are generally exempt with credit rather than technically zero-rated and require a valid customer VAT number, transport to another EU Member State, and proof of dispatch. Services are not automatically export zero-rated. Business-to-business services generally follow the customer-location rule and are invoiced without French VAT where the customer is established outside France, subject to reverse-charge or special place-of-supply rules. Special rules apply to services connected with immovable property, passenger transport, admission to events, transport-related services, short-term hiring, telecommunications, and other regulated categories. Input VAT refunds require valid VAT invoices, business-purpose evidence, and a properly filed VAT return or applicable non-established-business refund claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration containing the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs exit result or equivalent electronic proof that the goods exited the European Union customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, Incoterms where applicable, and export VAT treatment
Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or courier proof of delivery
Purchase order, sales contract, and accounting records linking the exported optical lenses or camera modules to the customs declaration
Evidence of exporter's customs representation and, where relevant, export authorization or product-control documentation
Bank payment or receivable records; an inward-remittance certificate is not generally a French statutory VAT-zero-rating document
For intra-Community supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT number, transport evidence, and required recapitulative statement or related reporting records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France does not impose a general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds as a condition of French VAT exemption. Export proceeds remain subject to ordinary accounting, anti-money-laundering, customs, and transfer-pricing controls, and banking institutions may request payment evidence. If export conditions are not substantiated, the DGFiP may reassess French VAT, deny or claw back input-VAT credits, assess late-payment interest generally calculated under Article 1727 of the French General Tax Code, and impose tax penalties. The penalty can generally be 40% for deliberate failure and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of law; lesser penalties may apply for other procedural or good-faith failures. False customs declarations may trigger customs duties, customs penalties, seizure or confiscation, and criminal exposure. Serious VAT fraud can result in criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment for responsible individuals. The taxpayer must retain invoices, customs records, transport evidence, payment records, and audit trails for the applicable statutory retention period, commonly at least six years for tax-accounting substantiation, subject to longer periods under customs, company-law, or litigation rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates within the Eurozone with full convertibility of the Euro on both capital and current accounts. No capital controls or FX surrender obligations exist for resident French entities. Profit remittances, capital repatriations, and all FX transactions are unrestricted subject only to standard corporate governance and AML compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the central bank. Receipts may be received in foreign currency and converted to EUR at market rates without statutory conversion ratios or timelines. Repatriation is immediate and unrestricted; funds may be held in foreign currency accounts provided they satisfy French reporting thresholds and full documentation requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI cross-border viability is moderate; offshore digital EMIs are feasible under French regulations but subject to strict ACPR oversight, licensing requirements, and enhanced AML/KYC controls that may limit direct offshore operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital KYC and account opening is fully permitted for corporate entities; physical presence or video interviews are not mandatory for standard onboarding but may be required for enhanced due diligence or high-value transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership in high-risk jurisdictions or shell company structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declarations, corporate structure charts, and source of wealth evidence

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent transaction patterns or unexplained large deposits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction narratives, export contracts, and proof of goods delivery

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections routed via SWIFT MT103 wires with purpose codes 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY INJECTION'. Verification requires board resolutions, capital increase filings, and bank statements; all transactions processed through correspondent networks with full audit trails.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements cleared via SWIFT MT103 for TT wires or Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) under UCP 600. Settlements in EUR or USD through correspondent banks; requires trade documentation including invoices, packing lists, and certificates of origin.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and reports (Comptes annuels) filed with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Guichet Unique)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months from fiscal year-end for shareholder approval; within 1 month of approval for registry filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil fine up to EUR 9,000 on legal representative; registry may send injunction and effect administrative strike-off after 3 months of non-action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, form 2065) with annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; 3 May following calendar-year close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 10%, increased to 40% after formal notice; monthly interest at 0.20%; no administrative strike-off consequence

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the register of beneficial owners (Déclaration RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via secured Infogreffe formality)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the time of annual accounts filing; within 30 days after any beneficial ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 30,000 and/or 6 months' imprisonment for concealment; continued failure can block accounts filing and trigger registry strike-off measures

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is mandatory for an SAS when at least two of three thresholds are exceeded: balance sheet total > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excl. VAT > EUR 8,000,000; average employees > 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) for individual statutory accounts; IFRS for consolidated accounts only when listed

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The legal representative files a sworn declaration confirming the accuracy of the RBE annually with the annual accounts deposit; any share transfer modifying beneficial ownership must be declared to the RBE within 30 days of signature of transfer
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $350 - $1,600 (market rate for professional registered office and agent services in France)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $6,000 - $18,000 (fee range for a statutory audit of a precision-optics manufacturing SAS subject to mandatory audit thresholds)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate under Art. 219 CGI; reduced 15% rate applies to the first €42,000 of taxable profit for SMEs satisfying Art. 219 I-b: turnover under €10 million and ≥75% owned by individuals)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME reduced rate 15% up to €42,000; R&D tax credit (Crédit d'impôt recherche, CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditures (up to €100m, 5% above); Innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% of eligible innovation expenditure for SMEs; patent box (Art. 238 CGI): 65% exemption of qualifying IP income, effective reduced rate 10%; territoriality of foreign PE profits (Art. 209 I, 2ème alinéa)
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No year limit (indefinite carryforward under Art. 209 CGI) with annual utilization cap of €1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable income exceeding €1,000,000; optional 1-year carryback (report en arrière) of up to €1,000,000

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (déclaration de résultats) plus annexes 2058-A to 2058-G (liaisse fiscale complète); mandatory electronic filing via the impots.gouv.fr professional portal using the EDI-TDFC (Édition et Dépôt Informatisé des Télé-Déclarations Fiscales et Comptables) or EFI (Échange de Formulaires Informatisé) teleprocedure
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (one definitive return per fiscal year; no quarterly instalment returns for IS, but quarterly prepayments of estimated tax are made via Form 2571 / 2571-SD by the 15th of March, June, September, December)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end (Art. 223 CGI); for a 31 December year-end, the filing deadline is the 2nd business day after 1 May (ordinarily 2-3 May) for EDI/EFI filers

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Résultat fiscal: bénéfice (taxable profit before the 25%/15% application and before loss carryforward)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only relevant where the non-resident company has a French permanent establishment (PE) treaty threshold analysis applies; otherwise no French IS return for pure offshore exports

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Résultat fiscal: déficit (tax loss of the year available for carryforward or carryback)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same as for residents; losses of a French PE can be carried forward against subsequent PE profits and optionally 1 year back

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Export turnover from precision optical lenses and camera modules (ISIC 2670), separated from French domestic turnover
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apportionment rules per PE; no export franchise for IS - worldwide turnover of a French PE is includible; report ex-works and destination-based net revenue

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Déductions: dépenses de R&D (R&D expenditure eligible for Crédit d'impôt recherche at 30% up to €100 million, 5% above)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: R&D must be physically performed in France (or in EEA under certain conditions); foreign subcontracting capped at 2x direct employee costs (Art. 244 quater B CGI)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impôt sur les sociétés at reduced 15%/25% rates; box for the amount taxable at the reduced rate (first €42,000 for SMEs and at 25% above)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 15% SME reduced rate is not available to entities whose 75% shareholder chain includes legal persons; non-resident-owned SAS commonly taxed at 25%

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Crédits d'impôt (CIR/CII) and impôt dû (net corporate tax after credits and prepayments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CIR refunds are available even where CIR exceeds the IS liability; non-resident-owned SAS should verify application of the anti-abuse rule for CIR monetization (a refund is blocked where the beneficial owner is outside EEA/France without substance)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic 10% increase of the tax due; 40% if the return is filed after a formal demand (mise en demeure); 80% in cases of overtly unlawful activity (activité occulte) or abusive behaviour (Art. 1728 CGI). Late payment interest: 0.20% per month (Art. 1727 CGI). Fixed penalty of €150 per omitted/incomplete annexed form (liaisse) with a minimum assessment; failure of the electronic obligation may attract a separate €15,000 fine (Art. 1738 CGI for non-respect of e-filing)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% on gross dividends paid to non-resident beneficial owners (Art. 119 bis 2 CGI); 0% exemption for qualifying EU/EEA parent companies under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (10% holding, 2-year minimum holding, subject to anti-abuse under Art. 119 ter CGI and the 2019 'CJEU/ATAD' substance case law); 75% punitive withholding for beneficiaries established in non-cooperative jurisdictions (Art. 238 A CGI)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: (i) To obtain treaty-reduced rate at source: the foreign shareholder must send to the French paying agent before payment a certificate of tax residence (Form 5000/5001/5002/5003 series for France; the DTA counterpart certificate issued by the beneficiary's tax authority), a declaration of beneficial ownership, and, where the DTA requires a holding period, evidence of the participation. (ii) If the full 30% is withheld, the non-resident may file a refund claim (demande de restitution) with the SIE/DRFIP of the paying company's location within the statutory claim window (normally by 31 December of the second year following the year of withholding) or, for EU residents, follow the EU dispute resolution/refund mechanisms. (iii) No TRC is sufficient alone — substance of the shareholder (economic activity in residence state) must be demonstrated where the anti-abuse clause or the MLI principal purpose test applies. (iv) Treaty rate framework: France applies the general DTA rates; e.g., France-China DTA 10%, France-Germany 15% portfolio/5% substantial, France-US 15% portfolio/5% substantial; the 2016 France-Germany protocol and the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive require a genuine establishment test before exemption/relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties/patent licence fees (Art. 182 B CGI): statutory domestic withholding 33.33% on sums paid to non-residents; relief by treaty (most French DTAs cap at 0% for patent royalties or 5-10% under OECD-based caps); EU Interest & Royalties Directive exemption for associated enterprises (25% shareholding held for at least 2 years, genuine establishment, no conduit). Interest: statutory rate generally 0% for non-resident lenders (Art. 125 A III CGI exemption), but a 75% punitive levy applies to interest, royalties and dividends paid to entities in non-cooperative jurisdictions (états non coopératifs) unless the payer demonstrates economic substance (Art. 238 A CGI). The 0% interest exemption is subject to arm's length recharacterization under Art. 57/CGI and the abuse-of-law procedure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full mandatory Local File + Master File (fichier local + fichier maître) where the French entity or the foreign-related group exceeds €400 million annual turnover (excl. taxes) or gross balance-sheet total (Art. L.13 AA LPF); Country-by-Country Report for groups with consolidated revenue ≥ €750 million (entity designated to file in France); companies below €400 million must nonetheless hold and produce simplified TP documentation on request within 30 days (Art. L.13 AB LPF)
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price Method (Méthode Comparable sur le Prix du Marché Libre – CUP)
Transactional Net Margin Method (Méthode de la Marge Nette Transactionnelle – TNMM)
Transactional Profit Split Method (Partage des Bénéfices)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) register comparable to the UAE/offshore regimes; instead substance is enforced through: (i) Article 57 CGI transfer pricing adjustment and recharacterization where the French SAS lacks personnel, premises and risk functions; (ii) the abuse-of-law doctrine (Art. L.64 LPF) allowing the tax authorities to disregard fictitious or sham transactions (including a shell SAS with a nominal registered office only); (iii) the shadow management (direction de fait) doctrine imposing director-level liability; (iv) the OECD BEPS principal purpose test applicable through French DTAs/MLI denying treaty benefits where transactions lack genuine economic substance; (v) Art. 238 A CGI requiring economic activity proof for payments to low-tax jurisdictions. For a precision-optics export SAS, substance means real head office, local management, order-taking and risk-bearing capacity in France, sufficient personnel and premises, and board/decision documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of taxable income — e.g., undisclosed offshore receivables from optical-lens exports, double invoicing, failure to file the 2065 return, or organized insolvency to evade IS (Art. 1741 CGI)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to €250,000 (basic); aggravated fraud (committed in an organized gang, involving money laundering, or with a fictitious company abroad) up to 7 years and €2,000,000; additional tax penalties up to 80% of the evaded tax plus 0.20% monthly late interest; mandatory publication of the conviction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director who orchestrates the fraud is prosecuted as perpetrator or accomplice (Art. 1742 CGI), with criminal fines and imprisonment; civil joint liability for the company's taxes and penalties; sursis to manage/ban from management (interdiction de gérer) up to 15 years; travel ban (interdiction de quitter le territoire) during investigation; asset freezing and confiscation orders

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Arrangement (Société fictive et abus de droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SAS registered in France without genuine economic substance — mailbox office, zero employees, all functions and risks performed by foreign related parties, artificial interposition purely to obtain French treaty benefits or the 15% reduced rate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Abuse-of-law procedure (Art. L.64 LPF): 80% penalty on the tax benefit and 0.20% monthly interest; recharacterization of transactions as taxable in France; treaty benefits denied under the principal purpose test; EUR penalties on VAT/IS/Git; possible dissolution of the vehicle
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil piercing against de facto or de jure directors (Art. L.651-1 et seq. Code de commerce) for comblement de passif if the sham causes insolvency; criminal sanctions for complicity in tax fraud (Art. 1741); interdiction de gérer; personal exposure to the 80% penalty where the director signed the abusive documentation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or present the Master File/Local File within 30 days of notice (Art. L.13 AA/L.13 AB LPF), submission of incomplete documentation, or deliberate use of non-arm's length margins for optical-lens exports to foreign affiliated distributors
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 5% of the reassessed amount where documentation is absent, insufficient or inaccurate (Art. 1735 CGI), without prejudice to the tax reassessment at the arm's length result; intérêts de retard at 0.20% per month; for CbCR: €100 per document and up to €15,000 per entity-related irregularity (implementing rules under Art. 1729 A CGI)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managerial fault (faute de gestion) allowing the civil receiver in bankruptcy to claim comblement de passif; personal fines if the director knowingly approved false documentation; for the shadow director (dirigeant de fait), same exposure; travel restrictions possible in judicial investigations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Defaults on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties or interest to non-resident owners/ licensees without deducting or remitting the 30% dividend WHT or the 33.33% royalty WHT, or without applying the DTA relief procedure properly
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French paying company is held liable for the unpaid withholding (Art. 1671 CGI) plus 5% penalty for late or deficient remittance and 0.20% monthly interest; where the beneficiary is in a non-cooperative state, the 75% punitive levy and the recharacterization of deductions under Art. 238 A apply
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly omitted the withholding face complicity proceedings for tax evasion (Art. 1741/1742), joint and several recovery of the withholding and penalties, criminal fines, and — in insolvency — an obligation to cover the company's tax shortfall; travel bans may be ordered during criminal investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering (Blanchiment de fraude fiscale) / AML Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring export proceeds through multijurisdictional shell accounts, irregular documentary letters of credit, or cash/Bitcoin settlements to conceal the tax base of the French SAS; failing suspicious transaction reporting and KYC on beneficial owners (medium-risk tier for precision optics)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering: up to 5 years' imprisonment and €375,000 fine; aggravated laundering (habitual, using professional activity, organized gang): 10 years' imprisonment and €750,000 fine; legal person (the SAS): fine up to 5 times the statutory fine and dissolution where founded for the purpose of laundering; confiscation of assets and freezing of accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors as beneficial owners and signatories are treated as principals; penalty includes confiscation of the optical-lens export business assets, interdiction de gérer (up to 15 years), travel bans and extradition exposure; personal criminal record plus exclusion from public procurement in the EU
